content:
If President Trump really wanted to see Kaitlan Collins smile, he should have tuned in to CNN last night.

The president's favorite reporter was beside herself with laughter on "The Source" last night as she covered an embarrassing self-own by Missouri Republican Senator Eric Schmitt during former special counsel Jack Smith's testimony the day before. Collins found Alabama Republican Senator Katie Britt's reaction to the hearing so amusing that she summed it up in one line.

"This easily ranks among the most classic moments in congressional testimony history," she said, laughing.

During the hearing, Schmitt asked Smith: "Did you go to the NBA game between the Golden State Warriors and the Atlanta Hawks on February 3, 2024?"

After Smith answered, puzzled, that he had not, Schmitt began explaining his question, noting the game was held in Atlanta — just one day after Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis admitted to an affair with another prosecutor, Nathan Wade. Willis was, like Smith, prosecuting Trump over his efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election.

Schmitt then presented what he believed was his smoking gun — a screenshot of a text from a member of Smith's staff, indicating Smith had attended a "Hawks" game that day.

But what Schmitt thought would be a slam dunk ended up looking more like an airball, because after several rounds of back-and-forth, Smith finally remembered that he had indeed attended a Hawks game that day — though not the Atlanta Hawks, and not even an NBA game.

He had gone to Maryland to watch a college women's basketball game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and the Maryland Terrapins, to see the then-rising star, now-WNBA player Caitlin Clark.

Progressive outlet MeidasTouch even located and shared footage of Smith at the Iowa-Maryland game on February 3, 2024, and HuffPost confirmed his identity through a spokesperson.

After airing several clips of Schmitt mixing up the Atlanta Hawks and the Iowa Hawkeyes on her CNN show — while barely containing herself — Collins asked her guest, Democratic strategist Paul Begala, what he made of the spectacle.

"Oh, poor baby, Senator Schmitt," Begala said mockingly, before adding an even more sarcastic note. "I'm glad they did that, okay? Because now you can see how brilliant Senator Schmitt's mind is."

"It's ridiculously stupid," Begala added. "And the whole thing is ridiculously stupid. There's 35 days until the election, gas is $4.50 a gallon, diesel is $6.50 a gallon, ground beef is $6.92 a pound... If you thought voters were ready for a change before this hearing, tired of the Republicans, they're going to be even more tired of them after this."

Collins's other guest, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton, echoed Begala's view, stressing that Republicans must focus on the cost of living ahead of the November midterms.

When Collins asked Singleton whether he thought Republicans should have brought Smith to testify, he responded in disbelief: "Why?! What do we get out of doing this?!”
